propositions: The inbound link differ is ADD-only by construction and does not emit removal records when a link is deleted in Jira, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating asymmetry.
A link deleted on the peer is never mirrored locally; it is re-added on the next pass due to outbound ADD semantics, converging to local-wins-and-restore behavior.
The apply layer discards non-add link records at apply_inbound_records.py:560-562, silently dropping any removal record before rebar.unlink can be called.

Arbitrating peer deletion from never-pushed local links requires persisted history of what the peer previously had; managed_refs alone cannot distinguish these identical states on every input the guards read.

Ecosystem research (Aha, Asana, Workfront, Exalate) shows link-deletion propagation is not commonly handled and risks inadvertent data loss; this behavior is deferred pending a per-binding baseline design proven on parent sync.
